first_impression.reaction: Sophie sent me this because I keep asking whether we really need 'an advisor' or whether she can book it all herself. The opening is sensible and doesn't talk down to me: 'quotes in Australian dollars and every inclusion confirmed in writing before you pay.' That's exactly the language I want to hear. And I like that it admits you can do it yourself, it's just slower. That's honest. I'll read the whole thing.

journey.quote: A good advisor is one person keeping all of it in step, with quotes in Australian dollars and every inclusion confirmed in writing before you pay.
journey.reaction: Yes. One person, AUD, in writing. That's three of my boxes ticked in one sentence.

journey.quote: Before you agree, ask any advisor about their fee in writing, inclusions, cancellation terms, insolvency cover and travel insurance.
journey.reaction: This is the list I'll copy out for Geoff. Insolvency cover is the thing I actually lie awake about, and I've never seen a wedding company mention it.

journey.section: What does a travel advisor actually do?
journey.quote: As at November 2026, Australian consumer guarantees give you rights if a travel service is delayed or cancelled, covering travel within Australia, travel departing Australia with international businesses, and travel to Australia booked through a provider's Australian website.
journey.reaction: Good that it's dated and points to the ACCC. It's a long sentence, though. I read it twice on the iPad before I understood it covers us flying out of Melbourne.

journey.section: One point of contact from flights to the ceremony
journey.quote: If the ceremony moves by a day, one conversation should flow through to flights, room nights and supplier bookings, rather than six separate emails from you.
journey.reaction: That's the picture I want. But 'should flow through' is a bit soft. And one contact during planning is one thing; who do I ring when we're actually over there and something goes wrong?

journey.quote: It turns a spreadsheet of euros, dollars and rupiah into one figure you can actually plan around.
journey.reaction: That's me. I'm the one with the spreadsheet. Very reassuring.

journey.section: Your consumer rights, booked either way
journey.quote: When you book through an agent, both the agent's terms and each provider's terms apply, and agents are usually bound by the provider's terms, so legally they may only need to pass on the remedy the provider offers.
journey.reaction: I appreciate the honesty, I really do. But this paragraph is heavy going. Am I reading it right that if the villa in Greece goes under, the agent may only pass on whatever the villa offers? Then what exactly protects our deposit? It raises the worry and doesn't quite settle it.

journey.section: What you can book yourself, and where it gets harder
journey.quote: **Who is tracking your guests?** Arrival dates, room allocations, dietary notes and the cousin who changes flights twice.
journey.reaction: Ha, we have that cousin. But my mother is 88 and uses a walking frame, and there's nothing here about older guests, transfers, or whether the venue is accessible. That's a real part of 'tracking guests' for us.

journey.section: Questions to ask before you hire an advisor
journey.quote: Insolvency insurance is not compulsory for agents, so only some hold it.
journey.reaction: Well, that's frank, and I'm glad to know it. Naturally my next question is whether Wedded Wonderland holds it, and the page doesn't say.

journey.section: Questions to ask before you hire an advisor
journey.quote: Some banks allow a chargeback if you do not receive what you paid for, and you should not accept contract terms that ask you to give up chargeback rights.
journey.reaction: Practical and grown-up. I didn't know that. Geoff will want to read this bit.

journey.section: Questions to ask before you hire an advisor
journey.quote: Read the Product Disclosure Statement before you buy, choose a policy that covers every country on the route including stopovers, and declare all pre-existing conditions upfront.
journey.reaction: Good, and the pre-existing conditions point matters for Mum and for Geoff's heart. Sensible advice, not salesy.

journey.section: When the trip is a wedding and a honeymoon
journey.quote: With [Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=travel-advisor-benefits&utm_content=primary), one Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact from start to finish, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD.
journey.reaction: Time zone and AUD are what I want. 'Anywhere in the world' is a big claim, but fine. Still no name, and I'd want to know who this Advisor is before Sophie signs anything.

journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and the advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: That's the sentence I was waiting for. I'd have liked it near the top, not at the very bottom.

unanswered_questions: Who would our Wedded Advisor be, by name, and can I have a phone call with them before anything is booked?
Who do we ring if something goes wrong at 2am Greek or Italian time once we're there?
How is the Wedded Wonderland fee worked out, and roughly what does it come to?
Does Wedded Wonderland hold insolvency insurance, and are deposits paid to overseas suppliers protected?
Are supplier contracts in English, and who signs them, us or Wedded Wonderland?
Can older guests with limited mobility be looked after with transfers and accessible rooms and venues?

turn_offs_found.quote: Under the guarantees, providers also do not have to offer a refund or replacement if you change your mind or miss a service for reasons unrelated to it. In those cases, it comes down to the booking's terms.
turn_offs_found.why: The consumer-rights section is a block of legal wording on an iPad. I follow it, but only just, and it leaves me more worried about deposits than when I started, without a plain line on what that means for us.

would_share_with: My husband Geoff, with the eight questions to ask before hiring an advisor
Sophie, to say the insurance and chargeback points are worth doing early

cta_reaction.quote: If you would like to talk through your wedding and honeymoon, [speak with Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=travel-advisor-benefits&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: 'Talk through' and 'speak with' sound like a person, which I want. I'd click if I knew it meant a phone call rather than a form, and I'd go in with the article's own questions about the fee, insolvency cover and deposits.

top_3_changes: Bring 'the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins' up near the top, beside the AUD and inclusions line, instead of leaving it to the last paragraph. It's the most reassuring sentence for the person paying.

Add older or less mobile guests to the 'Who is tracking your guests?' list (transfers, accessible rooms, getting to the ceremony), and a line on who to contact while you're actually away, so it isn't only about the planning months.

Give the consumer-rights section a plain one-line summary after the legal wording (for example, what it means for deposits you've paid), and break up the long sentences so they're easier to read on a tablet.
